one_to_two.input: one chain edge [x,y] and an incident elementary triangle {x,y,z} whose third vertex can be inserted without violating the declared simple-chain condition

two_to_one.input: consecutive chain edges [x,z],[z,y] bounding one elementary triangle with primitive third edge [x,y] and legal simplicity after deletion

terminal_one_to_one_pivot.input: terminal edge [x,y] and an incident side triangle {x,y,z}
terminal_one_to_one_pivot.output: replace terminal edge by [x,z], preserving the prefix through x
terminal_one_to_one_pivot.r1_reduction: this is exactly the AR incidence turn when x=O_E

paired_compensation: a disjoint 1->2 and 2->1 pair has net chain-count delta 0, but incidence alone does not select which sites must be paired or simultaneous
user_up_down_typing: Within the chain-cardinality interpretation, raw 1->2 is a literal +1 primitive-edge-count drift and raw 2->1 is -1. This realizes the earlier up/down intuition only for that carrier/length typing; it is not yet a carrier-independent native length theorem.
